content:
Since \(A\) is finite and \(\pi\) is onto \(A\), \(\pi\) must also be one-to-one. Thus \(\pi\) is a permutation of six elements.

Decompose \(\pi\) into disjoint cycles. An element in a cycle of length \(L\) returns to itself after six applications exactly when
\[
L\mid 6.
\]
Therefore every cycle length must be one of \(1,2,3,6\).

The number of permutations with cycle type
\[
1^{m_1}2^{m_2}3^{m_3}6^{m_6}
\]
is
\[
\frac{6!}{1^{m_1}m_1!\,2^{m_2}m_2!\,3^{m_3}m_3!\,6^{m_6}m_6!}.
\]

Now count each possible cycle type:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Cycle type} & \text{Number of permutations}\\ \hline
6 & \frac{6!}{6}=120\\
3+3 & \frac{6!}{3^2\cdot 2!}=40\\
3+2+1 & \frac{6!}{3\cdot2}=120\\
3+1+1+1 & \frac{6!}{3\cdot3!}=40\\
2+2+2 & \frac{6!}{2^3\cdot3!}=15\\
2+2+1+1 & \frac{6!}{2^2\cdot2!\cdot2!}=45\\
2+1+1+1+1 & \frac{6!}{2\cdot4!}=15\\
1+1+1+1+1+1 & 1
\end{array}
\]

Adding,
\[
120+40+120+40+15+45+15+1=396.
\]

\[
\boxed{396}
\]
